identifying the retroviral entity that may be involved in the causation of human breast tumors.
the possible role of exogenous retroviruses in breast cancer.
the possible role of exogenous retroviruses in the etiology of human breast cancer and human T-cell lymphoma.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have detected the same MMTV-like sequence in human breast tumors as has been previously reported, but in a much larger number of tumors.
the human breast tumor and lymphoma patient described herein is the first documented human case of a retroviral etiologic agent of cancer.
the presence of MMRV-like ENV sequences in a certain percentage (37%) of human breast tumors is consistent with an exogenous retrovirally etiology for these tumors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a certain percentage of breast tumors and T-cell lymphomas in humans may be caused by exogenous retroviruses.
the MMTV-like entity is a human virus and not a mouse virus.
the human genome contains MMTV-like elements, and that the human breast cancer genome contains MMTVs, which are capable of being amplified by PCR, sequenced, and hybridized.
